steps.text: 1. The user goes to Account → "Signed-in devices".
2. The system (Auth) returns the valid sessions: device name (e.g. "Chrome on Windows"), location, sign-in time, last activity.
3. The system shows the current device first with the "This device" label, the other devices by last activity. E1, E4.

exceptions.text: E1. Only the current device → the "Sign out all other devices" button is hidden.
E4. The list cannot be loaded → "The device list could not be loaded" with a Retry button.

steps.text: 4. The user taps "Sign out device" on another device. A1, A2.
5. The system asks "Sign out of <device name>?".
7. The system revokes the session, writes a revocation key in Redis, removes that row from the list and shows "Signed out <device name>". E2, E3.

exceptions.text: E2. The device is already signed out / expired or is not one's own → 404; the client shows "This device has already been signed out" and reloads the list.
E3. No network → "Cannot connect, please try again"; the other device's session does not change.

steps.text: 8. On the signed-out device, the next request is rejected (401); the client deletes the tokens and goes to Sign in with the message "The sign-in session has ended on this device".

exceptions.text: E5. A non-Admin viewing online devices → 403.
E6. Invalid device ID format → 400; invalid or expired token → 401.
E7. Redis does not respond → the online signal is ignored (still returns 204); the Admin only sees the number of signed-in devices with a note.

steps: A1.1. The user taps "Sign out all other devices" and confirms.
A1.2. The system revokes every session except the current one; the list only has "This device"; it shows "Signed out n devices".
A2. Sign out the device in use: the "Sign out" button on the Account page revokes the current session (UC#01 A6).

A3. The system signs out automatically: password reset (every device), password change (except the current device), suspension / ban (every device, UC#21), over 7 days without activity or 30 days since sign-in, reuse of an old refresh token, more than 100 sessions.
A4. New device alert: a sign-in on a device that never had a session → Auth publishes auth.new_device_login and Notification sends the email "New sign-in on <device>".
A5.1. Every client (signed in or not) sends an online signal every 60 seconds while the tab is visible or audio is playing, and sends a leave signal when the page closes. E6, E7.
A5.2. The Admin opens the "Online devices" page.

A5.3. The system shows the number of devices online (signed in and visitors), accounts online, signed-in sessions, devices that visited today / in 7 / 30 days and a table of signed-in devices that are online; it refreshes every 30 seconds. E5.
